new_task_1.title: Allow non-string hashable names in no-index stack operations
new_task_1.description: Stacking a Dataset or DataArray into a non-string hashable `new_dim` no longer fails immediately during variable stacking when xarray is not creating an index for that new dimension. The internal stack path now preserves the mapping form instead of requiring the new dimension name to be a keyword-compatible string.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `Dataset.stack()` and `DataArray.stack()` accept non-string hashable names for the new stacked dimension in stack flows that do not create an index, instead of failing early because the name is passed through Python keyword argument expansion.

expectation.grounded: When `stack()` is called with the mapping form of `dim` and the new dimension name is a hashable object that is not a string, the internal variable stacking path should pass that mapping through unchanged. If `create_index=False`, or if `create_index=None` results in no index being created, stacking should succeed and return an object whose stacked dimension uses that hashable name rather than raising `TypeError` from `**{new_dim: dims}` expansion.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to stack arrays into custom hashable dimension labels when they are not asking xarray to build an index for the new dimension. The stack operation should not impose an extra Python-keyword restriction beyond xarray's own dimension-handling rules.

constraints.grounded: This fix is limited to stack paths that do not create a stacked index. It does not by itself guarantee that non-string dimension names work in later index-building or MultiIndex creation code paths, so calls that still need index creation may continue to fail for those names until those paths are updated separately.
constraints.conceptual: Remove the premature keyword-argument failure without overstating support. No-index stack operations should improve, while existing limitations in index-producing stack modes may remain.

behavior: Dataset and DataArray stack operations no longer require the new stacked dimension name to be a Python keyword-compatible string when no index is being created.
The mapping form of `dim` is preserved through the internal stack implementation instead of being converted into keyword arguments.
Calls that previously failed immediately with `TypeError` at the variable stacking step can now complete in no-index stack modes.
acceptance_criteria: When `Dataset.stack()` is called with a mapping whose key is a non-string hashable and `create_index=False`, the stack operation should succeed instead of raising `TypeError` from keyword argument expansion.
When `DataArray.stack()` is called with a mapping whose key is a non-string hashable and `create_index=False`, it should return a stacked array whose stacked dimension uses that hashable name.
When `create_index=None` leads xarray not to create a stacked index for the requested dimensions, the same non-string hashable `new_dim` should be accepted.
When a stack call still goes through index or MultiIndex creation for the new dimension, existing failures in that later path are outside the scope of this fix and should not be silently masked.
